dev.subject: business-ocr
dev.text: Students regularly get this wrong in exams. Limited liability does NOT protect the business — the business can still go bust. What it protects is the owners. A shareholder who invested £5,000 can lose that £5,000 if the company collapses, but cannot be forced to sell their home to pay the company’s supplier invoices. With unlimited liability (sole traders and partnerships), creditors can. The mental image to hold is a wall between the shareholders’ personal money and the company’s debts. With Ltds and Plcs, that wall exists. With sole traders and partnerships, there is no wall.

dev.subject: geography-edexcel-b
dev.text: Soft engineering works with nature rather than against it. Beach replenishment (or nourishment) involves pumping sand from offshore onto eroding beaches. The wider beach absorbs wave energy and protects the cliffs behind. Bournemouth has replenished its beach roughly every five years since the 1970s; the cost is around £3 million per kilometre but the protection is renewable. Slope stabilisation uses drainage, replanting and netting to hold cliffs in place — effective at Lyme Regis, where deep drains were installed under the Black Ven landslide complex. Dune restoration plants marram grass to bind sand and trap it: the dunes at Studland Bay are stabilised using fenced walkways to keep walkers off.

dev.subject: cambridge-nationals-sport-studies
dev.text: The shift to all-seater grounds also changed the culture of watching football. Individual ticketing reduced the anonymity that could mask troublemakers, and CCTV coverage became far easier to implement. Crowd segregation — separating home and away supporters — was formalised. Together, these measures contributed to a significant fall in football-related disorder from the 1990s onwards.

dev.text: The amount of RAM a computer has directly affects how many programs it can run at once. If RAM fills up, the operating system must resort to virtual memory — using part of the secondary storage device as an overflow area. Because secondary storage is far slower than RAM, this causes a significant performance drop.

dev.text: Internal migration also reshapes the country. London continues to attract young workers in their twenties, while families in their thirties and forties increasingly leave the capital for cheaper towns in the south-east, the Midlands and South Wales — a process called counter-urbanisation. Retirees concentrate in coastal districts like North Devon, parts of East Yorkshire and the Welsh coast.

She had two festivals: one on 1 May, open to women of every class, and a far more exclusive nocturnal rite on 3 December, held at the house of a serving magistrate and led by the women of his household together with the Vestal Virgins.

dev.subject: health-social-care-ocr
dev.text: The nine person-centred values are not abstract ideals — when practitioners actually apply them, there are tangible, measurable benefits for two groups: the service providers who work in care settings and the service users who receive care. The specification asks you to know both sets of benefits and to be able to link them back to the values being applied. This is the key expectation for section 2.2: do not just list benefits in isolation; show how a specific value leads to a specific benefit for a named person or setting.

dev.subject: astronomy-edexcel
dev.text: The Solar System contains the Sun, eight planets, five recognised dwarf planets, and an enormous number of Small Solar System Objects (SSSOs). Understanding the distinctions between these categories — and where each type of body sits in the Solar System — is fundamental to understanding how the planetary system formed and evolved.

dev.subject: health-social-care-eduqas
dev.text: Albert Bandura’s social learning theory argues that much of human behaviour is learned through observation and modelling — watching others and imitating their behaviour, particularly when the model is admired or rewarded. Vicarious reinforcement occurs when an individual imitates a behaviour after observing someone else being rewarded for it, without being rewarded themselves. In adolescence, peer role models and social media influencers are particularly powerful models. A teenager who observes peers gaining social approval for a behaviour is more likely to imitate it — whether that behaviour is positive (volunteering, studying) or negative (smoking, risky behaviour). Social care practitioners working with young people in youth clubs or community settings use understanding of social learning to design positive role-model programmes.

dev.subject: l12-construction-built-environment
dev.text: Commercial buildings are used to provide services or retail products to customers and to accommodate business activities, typically undertaken to make a profit for their owners. Examples include shops, offices, banks, hotels and restaurants. Commercial buildings are usually adapted to fulfil the specific purpose of the business — a bank will have secure vaults; a restaurant will have a commercial kitchen. They may be purpose-built from scratch or converted from existing buildings to enable a change of use (for example, a Victorian warehouse converted into offices). Commercial buildings are often located in retail centres, town and city centres, or out-of-town retail parks where they can attract high customer footfall.

dev.subject: physical-education-edexcel
dev.text: Type IIa fibres (fast-twitch oxidative) represent an intermediate option. They contract faster than Type I fibres and produce more force, but they can also use aerobic metabolism when required. They fatigue more quickly than Type I but more slowly than Type IIx. They are dominant in activities requiring a sustained but high effort — 400 m and 800 m running, many team sports such as football and rugby where repeated bursts are interspersed with recovery periods.

dev.subject: history-edexcel
dev.text: G.W. Bernard’s The King’s Reformation (2005) emphasises Henry’s personal appetite for monastic wealth and his suspicion of any institution outside royal control. Diarmaid MacCulloch’s Thomas Cromwell: A Revolutionary Life (2018) argues Cromwell’s evangelical convictions made him a genuine reformer who saw monasticism as bad theology, not just rich theology — though he was happy to take the cash. The National Archives’ research guide stresses the long fiscal afterlife: the sales of the 1540s created a new gentry landowning class with a permanent stake in the Reformation. All three perspectives can be true at once.

dev.subject: psychology-edexcel
dev.text: The genetic explanation argues that addiction sometimes runs in families because of inherited biological factors, not only because family members share a home and habits. Simply showing that addiction clusters in families is not strong evidence on its own, because families also share their environment. Psychologists therefore turn to twin studies for stronger evidence. They compare the concordance rate of identical (monozygotic, or MZ) twins, who share 100% of their genes, with the concordance rate of non-identical (dizygotic, or DZ) twins, who share only around 50% of their genes. If MZ twins are more often concordant for addiction than DZ twins, this is taken as evidence that genes contribute to addiction risk, because the two twin types differ in genetic similarity but are assumed to share similarly close environments.

dev.subject: music-eduqas
dev.text: The front line usually consists of melody instruments such as trumpet, saxophone, trombone or clarinet, sometimes joined by a solo voice. They state the tune’s head (the main melody) at the start and end of a performance, and in between take turns improvising solos over the same repeating chord sequence, known as the changes.

dev.subject: drama-aqa
dev.text: In Puritan Salem, a person’s name is their social existence. Miller makes this explicit through Proctor’s refusal to sign his confession: the signed document will be nailed to the church door, making his false admission public property. What Proctor defends in refusing is not an abstract principle but his concrete identity — the legible record of who he has been in his community.

dev.subject: business-aqa
dev.text: A flat structure has few layers. A tech start-up of twenty people might have a founder, one team of engineers and one team of marketers — that’s it. Decisions are quick, staff feel trusted, and costs are lower because there are fewer managers to pay. The trade-off is that each manager supervises a lot of people, so they cannot give much individual attention.

dev.subject: economics-aqa
dev.text: Scarcity is the central economic problem: resources (land, labour, capital and enterprise) are limited, but human wants and needs are unlimited. Because of scarcity, all economic agents — consumers, producers and governments — must make choices about how to use resources.

dev.subject: citizenship-aqa
dev.text: Students should be aware that comparing political systems is a contested academic and political exercise, and that terms like “democracy” are themselves sometimes disputed. For exam purposes, the key is to present both viewpoints fairly and use specific evidence from both systems.

dev.subject: science-ocr-b
dev.text: Radiation is part of daily life. We are constantly exposed to background radiation from rocks (particularly granite), from cosmic rays from space, from radon gas in the air, from food and drink, and from medical procedures. This background dose varies by location — living in Cornwall exposes you to more radon than living in London, because granite rock releases more of this naturally occurring radioactive gas.

dev.subject: drama-aqa
dev.text: Every director mounting Romeo and Juliet faces a fundamental interpretive question: how should the performers engage with Shakespeare’s heightened verse? One answer is to treat the play with the full apparatus of psychological realism: the performers research their characters’ inner lives, find the emotional truth beneath every line, and attempt to make even the most formal iambic pentameter feel as natural as a contemporary conversation. The other answer is to lean into the play’s artifice: accept that this is a ritual theatrical form, use the verse as a heightened, stylised vocal score and place the action in a world where the elevated language is the natural language of passion and grief.

dev.subject: it-ocr
dev.text: Key risks include: data interception (a hacker captures health data transmitted by a wearable device); unauthorised device control (a smart lock or vehicle control system accessed by an attacker); privacy violation (always-on microphones or cameras collect and transmit data that could be exposed in a breach); and cascading attacks (compromising one IoE device gives an attacker a foothold to move across an entire connected network). In safety-critical applications such as emergency services or hospital equipment, a successful attack could have life-threatening consequences.

dev.subject: film-studies-eduqas
dev.text: The opening car-door sequence sets the film’s tonal register immediately. The scene closes with Lady Bird opening the passenger door and tumbling onto the roadside verge — a moment staged entirely without comment, the mise-en-scene returning in a single cut to the two women walking silently into the school. The comedy of the physical action and the silence of the aftermath together communicate the relationship’s rhythm: explosive, then quickly resumed. Cinematographer Sam Levy holds a mid-range two-shot for the car conversation, keeping both women visible in the same frame — a Gerwig compositional signature that refuses to privilege one perspective over the other.

dev.subject: design-technology-eduqas
dev.text: Choosing the wrong paper or board for a product leads to failure — a flimsy cereal carton that cannot survive stacking in a warehouse, a point-of-sale display that buckles under its own weight, or packaging whose surface absorbs ink and blurs the brand logo. Designers must balance several competing factors every time they specify a material: function (will it do the job?), aesthetics (does it look and feel right?), cost (is it within budget?), availability (can it be sourced in the right stock form?), and environmental and ethical considerations (is it sustainably sourced and responsibly produced?). These factors rarely point to the same material, so selection always involves a reasoned compromise.

He took the argument further in his later book Social Theory and Social Structure. Merton argued that deviance results from the culture and structure of society — not from individual pathology or moral failure.

holdout.subject: food-preparation-and-nutrition-eduqas
holdout.text: Inadequate food hygiene causes food wastage as well as illness. Food that has been contaminated or allowed to spoil must be discarded, representing a financial loss to households and businesses. On a wider scale, food waste contributes to greenhouse gas emissions — particularly methane from organic matter decomposing in landfill. WRAP estimates that UK households wasted food and drink worth about £1,000 per household of four in 2022. In a commercial kitchen, a food-poisoning outbreak can result in closure by environmental health officers, significant fines, reputational damage and civil claims from affected customers — consequences that far exceed the small cost of correct food handling.

holdout.subject: film-studies-eduqas
holdout.text: The closing sequence of The Farewell uses a single sustained slow-motion family walk through the streets of Changchun. Solano holds the wide frame, and the slow motion extends the duration of a gesture — the family together in a public street — that would otherwise be entirely ordinary. The non-diegetic score (Alex Weston) enters here for one of its rare appearances, gentle and unhurried, coding the sequence as elegiac rather than triumphant. The slow motion does not aestheticise the family as a spectacle; it gives the ordinary act of walking together an emotional weight that the rest of the film’s formal restraint has been building toward.

A modern washing machine uses a microcontroller to time wash cycles, monitor water temperature via a thermistor, detect an unbalanced drum via an accelerometer, and control the motor speed — all in a single chip. Without reprogrammability, manufacturers would need to produce different circuit boards for each wash programme (delicates, cottons, quick wash) instead of a single board with different software settings.

holdout.text: Not all aims are purely financial. Customer satisfaction is a central aim for many retailers. A pharmacy chain may train all staff in product advice and offer a consultation service not because it directly boosts today's profit, but because satisfied customers return and recommend the business to others. Brand reputation sits alongside this — a retailer with a strong, trusted brand can charge a premium and withstand occasional negative press more easily than one with a weak identity. A premium department store, for example, carefully manages visual merchandising, staff presentation and returns policies because every interaction either builds or damages the brand.

Seneca writes about the sounds and distractions of a noisy bath complex from the viewpoint of a writer trying to concentrate. holdout.subject: history-eduqas
holdout.text: The question of whether Elizabethan England was a ‘Golden Age’ is one of the central debates in the study of this period. The label was applied enthusiastically by Victorian historians who admired the Armada’s defeat, Shakespeare’s plays and the dramatic expansion of English trade and exploration. It has been challenged by later historians who pointed to poverty, religious intolerance, social inequality and unresolved political problems. Your task in an extended essay is not to pick one side, but to weigh the evidence carefully and reach a substantiated judgement.

holdout.subject: food-preparation-and-nutrition-eduqas
holdout.text: Some nutrients depend on other nutrients to work properly. Three important complementary pairs: (1) Vitamin C and iron — vitamin C in the small intestine converts ferric iron (from plant sources) to ferrous iron, which is absorbed more efficiently. Adding lemon juice to a lentil dish or drinking orange juice with cereal are practical examples. (2) Vitamin D and calcium — vitamin D promotes the production of calcium-binding proteins in the gut wall, enabling calcium to be absorbed into the bloodstream. Without adequate vitamin D, dietary calcium largely passes through unabsorbed. (3) B vitamins working together — several B vitamins act as coenzymes in the same metabolic pathways; a deficiency in one can impair the action of another. Understanding these complementary actions is required by the spec and often tested in extended response questions about planning diets for specific individuals.

It cannot date rocks at all because rocks do not contain significant amounts of organic carbon.

holdout.subject: astronomy-edexcel
holdout.text: Capture Theory proposes that the Moon formed elsewhere in the solar system and was gravitationally captured when it passed close to Earth. A major problem is that capture requires the Moon to slow down dramatically at precisely the right moment — the gravitational physics make this very unlikely without a mechanism to dissipate energy. Co-accretion Theory suggests the Moon and Earth formed simultaneously from the same disc of material orbiting the young Sun. This struggles to explain the Moon's low density and small iron core compared to Earth. The Giant Impact Hypothesis addresses both problems and remains the dominant scientific model.

holdout.subject: engineering-aqa
holdout.text: Soft soldering uses a filler metal with a melting point below 450 °C — traditionally a tin-lead alloy, now typically lead-free tin-copper or tin-silver for health reasons. The soldering iron heats the joint; flux is applied to remove oxide films and allow the solder to flow; the filler melts and fills the gap by capillary action. The parent metal does not melt. Soft solder is used for electronic circuit-board connections and for joining copper water pipes (plumbing). The joint is weaker than the parent metal and not suitable for structural applications.

holdout.text: The frontier is usually drawn as a curve bowing outwards rather than a straight line. This shape reflects the law of increasing opportunity cost: as you transfer more and more resources from producing consumer goods to capital goods, each extra unit of capital goods costs a progressively larger sacrifice of consumer goods. This happens because resources are not perfectly suited to every type of production — a baker transferred to an engineering factory is initially less productive there.

holdout.text: The Roman Senate was, like the Athenian assembly, an exclusively male body. Roman women could not vote in the popular assemblies, stand for magistracies, or sit in the Senate. Yet Roman women — particularly those of the aristocracy — had more daily freedom of movement than their Athenian counterparts. They attended dinner parties alongside their husbands, visited temples and public spaces, and were visible in the life of the city in a way that respectable Athenian women were not.
